meta.title: Getting between town and airport, and a passenger's choices when a flight is canceled or badly delayed
meta.builtOn: src/engine/content/air.ts keeps taxi flat fares at JFK, LAX, LHR (Heathrow Express), YVR, ATL and MSY, and GO Airport Shuttle New Haven to JFK/LGA from $79. This file adds every other option found, and re-reads the ones SLATE keeps.
meta.confirmedMeans: confirmed:true only when the figure was read on the operator's or the authority's own page on 2026-10-02. A figure from a search summary, a third-party guide, or a summary of a blocked page is confirmed:false.
meta.nullMeans: fare or minutes null: not found on a page that could be read; never estimated here.

rebooking.rule: Applies to flights departing an EU airport, and to flights arriving in the EU on an EU carrier. Cancellation: Article 5. Long delay: Article 6. Denied boarding: Article 4.

choices.trigger: Cancellation; or departure delay of 5 hours or more (Art. 6(1)(iii), refund option only); or denied boarding.
options: (a) reimbursement within seven days of the full cost of the ticket at the price paid, for parts not made and parts made if the flight no longer serves its purpose, plus where relevant a return flight to the first point of departure
(b) re-routing, under comparable transport conditions, to the final destination at the earliest opportunity
(c) re-routing, under comparable transport conditions, to the final destination at a later date at the passenger's convenience, subject to availability of seats

byDistance.note: also all intra-EU flights over 1,500 km

cancellationNoticeExemptions: told at least 14 days before departure: no compensation
told 7-14 days before and re-routed to depart no more than 2 hours early and arrive less than 4 hours late: none
told under 7 days before and re-routed to depart no more than 1 hour early and arrive less than 2 hours late: none
compensation.delay: Arrival 3 hours or more late carries the same compensation (CJEU Sturgeon, C-402/07 and C-432/07, 2009); not in the EU text itself.
compensation.extraordinaryCircumstances: No compensation if the carrier proves extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided even if all reasonable measures had been taken.
compensation.paidAs: cash, bank transfer or cheque; travel vouchers only with the passenger's signed agreement

care.delayThresholds: 2 hours or more for flights up to 1,500 km; 3 hours or more for 1,500-3,500 km and intra-EU over 1,500 km; 4 hours or more otherwise. Always for cancellations.
provided: meals and refreshments in reasonable relation to the waiting time
hotel accommodation where a stay of one or more nights becomes necessary
transport between the airport and the accommodation
two telephone calls, telex or fax messages, or e-mails

rebooking.note: Amounts, Art. 8 choices and Art. 9 care read from EUR-Lex and the parallel UK text. A revision was agreed by Parliament and Council on 15 June 2026 and approved by MEPs on 7 July 2026 (646-12), reportedly keeping the 3-hour threshold and the €250/€400/€600 grid (search summaries, confirmed:false); its in-force date and other changes are worth checking.

rebooking.rule: Applies to flights departing a UK airport, and to flights arriving in the UK on a UK or EU carrier. Same structure as the EU text, amounts in sterling.

choices.trigger: Cancellation; departure delay of 5 hours or more (refund option); denied boarding.
options: (a) reimbursement within seven days of the full cost of the ticket at the price at which it was bought
(b) re-routing, under comparable transport conditions, to the final destination at the earliest opportunity
(c) re-routing, under comparable transport conditions, to the final destination at a later date at the passenger's convenience, subject to availability of seats

compensation.delay: Art. 6(3): 'In case of a delay of three hours or more in reaching the final destination, the passengers concerned have the right to compensation laid down in Article 7.' Inserted 14 December 2023 by the Aviation (Consumers) (Amendment) Regulations 2023 (SI 2023/1370), so the UK has the Sturgeon rule in statute.
compensation.cancellationNoticeExemptions: As the EU: 14 days; 7-14 days with re-routing (depart ≤2 h early, arrive <4 h late); under 7 days with re-routing (depart ≤1 h early, arrive <2 h late).
compensation.extraordinaryCircumstances: No compensation if the carrier proves extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided even if all reasonable measures had been taken.

care.delayThresholds: 2 hours (≤1,500 km), 3 hours (1,500-3,500 km), 4 hours (otherwise); hotel when the new departure is at least the day after.
provided: meals and refreshments in reasonable relation to the waiting time
hotel accommodation where one or more nights' stay becomes necessary
transport between the airport and the accommodation
two telephone calls, telex or fax messages, or e-mails

rebooking.note: Articles 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 read on legislation.gov.uk (each at /eur/2004/261/article/N).

rebooking.jurisdiction: US (DOT automatic refund rule, 14 CFR Part 260, final rule April 2024; FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024)
rebooking.rule: A passenger is owed a refund when the airline cancels or significantly changes a flight and the passenger does not accept the alternative transportation or travel credit offered. There is no federal cash compensation for delays or cancellations.

options: accept the airline's rebooking or alternative transportation
accept a travel credit or voucher (only if the passenger chooses it)
decline both and receive an automatic cash refund to the original form of payment
significantChange: domestic flight departing 3 or more hours earlier or arriving 3 or more hours later than scheduled
international flight departing 6 or more hours earlier or arriving 6 or more hours later than scheduled
change of departure or arrival airport
downgrade to a lower class of service
connections at different airports, or a less accessible aircraft or connecting airport for a passenger with a disability
choices.refundTiming: within 7 business days for credit-card purchases; within 20 calendar days for other forms of payment
choices.refundForm: cash or the original form of payment, not vouchers unless the passenger chooses them

compensation.note: None required by federal rule. DOT withdrew in 2025 the proposed rule that would have required compensation (from $200) for controllable disruptions (search summary, confirmed:false). Compensation is owed only for involuntary denied boarding (14 CFR 250, not researched here).
compensation.bagFee: Checked-bag fee refunded if a mishandled-bag report is filed and the bag is not delivered within 12 hours of a domestic flight's arrival at the gate, or 15-30 hours for an international flight depending on flight length.
compensation.ancillary: Fees for extra services paid for and not provided (wifi, seat selection, inflight entertainment) are refunded.

care.note: No federal requirement for meals or hotels. Large US airlines' own commitments are on DOT's Airline Customer Service Dashboard (not read here).

rebooking.effective: Key automatic-refund provisions from 16 May 2024 (FAA Reauthorization Act); remaining provisions from 28 October 2024.
rebooking.note: transportation.gov refunds page returned 403 and ecfr.gov redirected to a block page; all of this is from search summaries of DOT's own pages. Rules are well established but not read first-hand on 2026-10-02.

rebooking.rule: Flights to, from and within Canada. Obligations depend on whether the disruption is within the airline's control, within its control but required for safety, or outside its control.

rebookingLargeCarrier: the next available flight operated by the airline or a partner, from the original airport, on a reasonable route
if that would not depart within 9 hours of the original departure: a flight on any airline, including non-partners, from the same airport
if nothing can be found within 48 hours (outside-control disruptions): any airline, from any nearby airport
choices.rebookingSmallCarrier: the next available flight operated by the airline or a partner from the same airport
choices.refund: If the alternative is unacceptable to the passenger, or the trip no longer serves its purpose, a refund of the unused portion (and the used portion if no purpose), to the original form of payment; for within-control disruptions, the passenger who declines the alternative also gets the minimum compensation $400 (large) / $125 (small).

categories.withinControl: rebooking or refund, standards of treatment, compensation
categories.withinControlSafety: rebooking or refund, standards of treatment, no compensation

compensation.trigger: Disruption within the airline's control and not required for safety, notified less than 14 days before departure, arrival 3 or more hours late.
compensation.largeCarrierDefinition: transported 2 million or more passengers worldwide in each of the two preceding years (Air Canada, WestJet, Porter, Flair, Air Transat, Sunwing per CTA)
compensation.form: money (cash, cheque, transfer) by default; vouchers only if the passenger chooses and they are worth more
compensation.claim: file with the airline within one year; airline has 30 days to pay or explain (search summary)

care.trigger: Within-control disruptions (including safety-related) after a 2-hour wait.
provided: food and drink in reasonable quantities
access to a means of communication
hotel or comparable accommodation and transport to it when an overnight wait is needed
care.note: Care thresholds from the regulation as commonly stated; the CTA page fetched did not quote them.

rebooking.note: Categories, rebooking tiers, compensation table and money-by-default read on the CTA's own page. Refund detail, claim deadline and care thresholds are not quoted from it (worth checking). Amending regulations (Canada Gazette I, 21 December 2024) would drop the three categories in favour of compensation unless 'exceptional circumstances', with the burden on the airline; their entry into force was not confirmed by 2026-10-02.

rebooking.jurisdiction: Mexico (Ley de Aviación Civil, art. 47 Bis, with art. 52)
rebooking.rule: Domestic and international flights by Mexican concessionaires/permit holders, for delays and cancellations attributable to the airline.

choices.trigger: Cancellation attributable to the airline, or delay over 4 hours (treated as cancellation).
options: refund of the ticket price (or of the unflown portion) plus compensation of at least 25% of the ticket price
transport on the first available flight, with meals, lodging when an overnight stay is needed, and ground transport to and from the lodging
transport at a later date convenient to the passenger, plus compensation of at least 25% of the ticket price

delayTiers.owed: compensation under the airline's own published policy: discounts on future flights, or food and non-alcoholic drinks
